nodes.label: Precomputed values and simplifying repetitive code

edges.label: The topic 'Precomputed values and simplifying repetitive code' introduces lookup_table.
Space-time tradeoff is taught under "Precomputed values and simplifying repetitive code".

[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: saving results is always better, and storing data is free. Rule: precomputation spends memory proportional to the number of saved values to save time, which pays off only when values are reused and the table fits in memory.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: a space-time tradeoff invests memory (an array of saved values) to save computation time.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: by investing in space (saving values) we save time (no recomputation). PrimeSieve trades a boolean array of size N for speed over the two-variable trial-division method.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: a precompute phase (one pass storing N values) runs first, then a use phase in which each query is one array read.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: the same answers as recomputation, using about N extra memory cells and much less time per query.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: during precomputation each step stores one value in the table; during use each lookup changes nothing.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The lookup table is the stored space: each value is computed once and then read by index.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: speed up programs that need the same values many times (harmonic numbers, primes up to N).

[0] predict_a_change (C): Conservation: results are unchanged by precomputing. Memory grows linearly with N, so for huge N or for values used only once the tradeoff stops paying.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: precompute when the values are needed for small N many times and memory is ample. Recompute when N is huge, memory is tight, or each value is used once.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The table must fit in the memory Java allows. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: N too large for the array (OutOfMemoryError, or NegativeArraySizeException if N+1 overflows)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Precomputation pays only when values are reused. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: a huge table is built for a single query, so the program is slower and larger with no benefit
Saved values are read back by index, H[i], instead of being recomputed.
Saving precomputed values in an array trades memory for time: each value is computed once and then looked up.
